- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.18) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 7-day mean), model often overshoots; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 3–5 days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 10-day moving average), model overreacts; apply downward bias of 1–4%.
- When sentiment is high (≥0.44) and model forecasts are rising, check for overconfidence; cap upward momentum at 2–3% above recent peak.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period volatility; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment is volatile or recent price range is wide.
- If true outcome deviates >5% from 14-day moving average, model is lagging; adjust forecast to align with 14-day trend, especially if sentiment is neutral or rising.
